"""Build the batching comparison report (seeds 0-9, sizes 1 and 16)."""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from run import arrivals, latencies, summarize

SEEDS = range(10)
WORKLOADS = ("sparse", "burst")


def build():
    runs = []
    for seed in SEEDS:
        for w in WORKLOADS:
            times = arrivals(seed, w)
            s1 = summarize(latencies(times, 1))
            s16 = summarize(latencies(times, 16))
            runs.append({"seed": seed, "workload": w, "requests": len(times),
                         "size_1": s1, "size_16": s16,
                         "mean_delta_ms": s16["mean_ms"] - s1["mean_ms"],
                         "p95_delta_ms": s16["p95_ms"] - s1["p95_ms"]})
    return runs


def conclusion(runs):
    parts = []
    for w in WORKLOADS:
        r = [x for x in runs if x["workload"] == w]
        m1 = sum(x["size_1"]["mean_ms"] for x in r) / len(r)
        m16 = sum(x["size_16"]["mean_ms"] for x in r) / len(r)
        better = sum(x["mean_delta_ms"] < 0 for x in r)
        parts.append(f"{w}: {r[0]['requests']} requests/seed, {len(r)} seeds; mean latency "
                     f"size 1 = {m1:.2f} ms, size 16 = {m16:.2f} ms; size 16 lower in "
                     f"{better}/{len(r)} seeds")
    return ("Hypothesis only partly supported. " + "; ".join(parts) +
            ". Batching 16 reduces latency in the burst workload (queueing at size 1 dominates) "
            "but increases it in the sparse workload, where 40 ms spacing means each request waits "
            "the 20 ms batch timeout. The sparse trace has 31 requests, not 32 (index 17 is a "
            "modeled missing telemetry sample); the burst trace has 32.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    runs = build()
    out = Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "build/batching.json")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps({"runs": runs, "conclusion": conclusion(runs)}, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(out)
EOF
